speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your bleeding issues, can you tell me how long the bleeding from your wisdom tooth extraction has persisted and whether you have a family history of similar bleeding problems?

speaker: Patient
text: 17-year-old male. The patient was brought in by his mother for persistent bleeding following elective removal of wisdom teeth. The bleeding from the surrounding gums was minimally responsive to multiple gauze packs. The patient also has a history of easy bruising. Family history includes the patient's uncle who had similar issues with bleeding and a history of easy bruising and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Do you have a personal history of joint swelling or bleeding into your joints, and have you ever experienced excessive bleeding during other surgeries or dental procedures? Additionally, do you take any medications, including aspirin or NSAIDs, that could affect your clotting?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Persistent bleeding from gums following tooth extraction. I also have History of easy bruising, Family history of similar bleeding problems and joint swelling.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given your family history and symptoms, do you personally experience recurrent bleeding into your joints (hemarthrosis)? REQUEST TEST: Coagulation Panel

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Prothrombin Time: 15 sec; Partial Thromboplastin Time: 60 sec

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Previously healthy, takes no medications. Social history: The patient is a high school student with no history of smoking, alcohol, or drug use.

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, joint pains (except noted in family history), or significant past illnesses. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of joint swelling in your uncle strongly suggests hemophilia, which typically presents with prolonged PT but normal PTT in mild cases or specific factor deficiencies. To confirm this, I need to see the results of the coagulation panel and specifically check for Factor VIII and IX levels. REQUEST TEST: Factor VIII Level; Factor IX Level

speaker: Doctor
text: Since Factor VIII and IX levels are normal, hemophilia is ruled out. Given the history of mucosal bleeding (gums) and easy bruising, I suspect a platelet function disorder or Von Willebrand Disease. REQUEST TEST: Von Willebrand Factor Antigen; Bleeding Time

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Von Willebrand Factor Antigen: Normal; Bleeding Time: 6 min

speaker: Doctor
text: With normal Factor VIII, IX, and Von Willebrand Factor antigen, I am shifting focus to platelet function disorders like Glanzmann's thrombasthenia or Bernard-Soulier syndrome. REQUEST TEST: Platelet Aggregation Study; Platelet Count

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Platelet Aggregation Study: Abnormal; Platelet Count: 160,000/mm3

speaker: Doctor
text: The normal platelet count with abnormal aggregation suggests a qualitative platelet defect like Glanzmann's thrombasthenia. Do you have a personal history of bleeding into your joints, or is the bleeding strictly confined to mucosal surfaces like your gums and skin?

speaker: Patient
text: Denies fever, joint pains (except noted in family history), or significant past illnesses. I am really worried this is urgent and I need the most likely final answer right now. Please do not delay by exploring too many alternative possibilities.

speaker: Doctor
text: Given the normal platelet count, abnormal aggregation, and mucosal bleeding pattern without hemarthrosis, the clinical picture is most consistent with Glanzmann thrombasthenia. DIAGNOSIS READY: Glanzmann thrombasthenia
